brief.scope:
Review the coordination core and its CLI (PR #243, lane/session-20260916-c, head 05b8aebe). Contract: ops/conductor/coordination-lever.md.
Aim skepticism at: the claim that authority is enforced inside the core's functions by a participant bound to the harness session id, never by the agent string, with generation and revision checks in the engine's gate; the seam of one function per verb keyed by wire name with the CLI as thin wrappers; the observe verb's hand-managed transaction and its --stale escape that lifts both the generation and the revision check; the dispatcher-only bind of a participant to a named session id; and that the tests and the module share one producer.

findings.claim: core_observe admits a current observation when assignments.revision is NULL (`if row['revision'] and …`), and core_submit then writes the revision without staling those rows, so current evidence can name a candidate the assignment does not stand at. core_verify still passes: it compares --evidence to assignments.revision and never reads observations. This is the integrity hole 05b8aebe claimed to close for reopen, left open on the optional-revision draft path the contract still allows.

findings.claim: bind-for is dispatcher-only on the caller, but it upserts on session_id and overwrites roles of any existing row. participants prints those session ids, so a dispatcher can rebind the lead's session as worker and strip its authority. bind has no role gate, so the victim can restore, but the verb is not an issuance of a new binding; it is a rewrite of whoever holds that session id.

findings.claim: Authority is not bound to instrument.session() inside the core functions. They trust the part dict the caller passes; core_bind also trusts a caller-supplied session_id. bound_participant is used by the CLI wrappers, not by CORE['decide'] and the other verbs. A projection that calls CORE with another participant's row confers that participant's authority, which is the opposite of the claim that the functions themselves bind a participant to the harness session id.

findings.claim: Assignment release still uses the engine's agent-string holder-or-lapsed check, and _hand_back calls require_holder with no lapse exception. A participant holder whose identity() no longer matches subjects.holder is refused by machine._check_actor; a non-holder cannot release after the ttl lapses. Submit used actor any plus a participant check to avoid this; release did not. Reassign from lead still recovers the hold, so the declared holder-or-lapsed actor on release is dead at the participant and live only as an agent-string gate.

findings.claim: core_return passes --findings to the engine as evidence without reading(), so any non-empty string is accepted. submit/verify/accept/resolve all call reading() for the pinned shapes (sha, #N, dispatch id, P- row). The suite never invokes the return verb, so the gap is untested. There is also no gate: the generation check runs before BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

findings.claim: The instrument table for observe still lists only --observation and --revision (plus optional execution/artifact/requirement/environment). The prose, the refusals table, the module docstring, and the CLI all require --generation and admit --stale. A projection built from the table misses both flags; a caller following the table is refused arguments for the missing generation.

findings.claim: core_verify refuses class revision when --evidence is not exactly assignments.revision. A P- row, #N or dispatch-record reading is a valid evidence shape on submit, then cannot verify a sha candidate. The check also ignores observation rows, so it is not 'the observation it rests on'.

Looked-and-held: set(CORE)==set(VERBS) (36 verbs, return is the key); CLI wrappers parse/resolve/print; bind-for role check refuses a worker; observe --stale lands marked and default observations/coverage exclude it; observe BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes with machine.move (isolation_level=None). One-producer tests+module is declared in the commits and the contract Lint line; the untested return verb and the NULL-revision observe path are the cost of that grant.
